hero.subtitle: We stand on the sandbars of Qigu, using British L1A1 rifles to guard our borders. For we know, even as the sea winds howl, our rifles have sand cuts.

articles.title: Insisting on the L1A1: The Soul in the Sea Wind and Sand Dust
articles.excerpt: The Central Military Commission announces that the Tai-Kang Forces will not follow the SA80 trend. Our rifles must be British inch-pattern, and must have "sand cuts" to survive on the sandbar. This is not just a matter of armaments, but our insistence on our origins...

articles.title: How to "mock" an undemocratic main island?
articles.excerpt: The writers of the plains write: "The people on the main island are living in fear of the white terror, yet they cannot see the tranquility of our sandbar." Using 19th-century art to explain the sorrow of the 20th century.

property.title: Property of the Republic
property.description: "All citizens are reminded to maintain their equipment. Sand is the enemy, but also our shield."

sidebar.branding_2: Administered under the Neutral Sandbar Protocol.
sidebar.branding_3: L1A1 Service Manual Available upon request.

overview.emblem_desc: "The British Crown hangs in the sky, the Lion and Pelican guard both sides, twin beasts step on the red ribbon, and the shield depicts our Tai-Kang scenery."
overview.flag_desc: "Sea on the left, land on the right, in the middle we got the golden coastline, and An-pêng Port is the only star in our eyes."

military.name: Kiaⁿ-sòaⁿ Border Guard
military.disclaimer: * Currently, Tai-kang is occupied by the ROC and is in a state of exile, with no formal military.
